name: membarrier
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_membarrier, int cmd, unsigned int flags, int cpu_id);
description: The membarrier() system call reduces the overhead of memory barriers in multi-threaded applications by allowing replacement of barriers on frequently executed paths with compiler barriers and using membarrier on less frequent paths. It ensures memory accesses match program order for targeted threads, improving performance on multi-core systems.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: The command to execute, such as MEMBARRIER_CMD_QUERY, MEMBARRIER_CMD_GLOBAL, or others

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for the command, typically set to 0

parameters.name: cpu_id
parameters.description: CPU ID for specific commands, if applicable

return_value.success: Returns a bit mask for MEMBARRIER_CMD_QUERY, or 0 for other commands
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: cmd is invalid, or flags is nonzero, or certain commands are disabled
The membarrier() system call is not implemented by the kernel
The current process was not registered prior to using private expedited commands

examples: static int membarrier(int cmd, unsigned int flags, int cpu_id) { return syscall(__NR_membarrier, cmd, flags, cpu_id); }
static void slow_path(int *read_a) { b = 1; membarrier(MEMBARRIER_CMD_GLOBAL, 0, 0); *read_a = a; }
